references.text: Moses sat to judge the people, and the people stood before him from morning until evening, illustrating how one came before Moses with their cases.
The entrance to the tabernacle (the tent of meeting) was where the Lord met with his people, the same place where the daughters of Zelophehad stood.
A case is brought before Moses for a decision, just as the daughters of Zelophehad came to Moses with their case.
Those who found a man gathering wood on the Sabbath brought him before Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation, similar to the situation with the daughters of Zelophehad.
It mentions the entrance to the tabernacle where the entire congregation was gathered, the same place where the daughters of Zelophehad stood.
Eleazar the priest is mentioned as the one who should stand before the Lord to receive counsel, and he is also noted in verse 2 where the daughters of Zelophehad came forward.
The daughters of Zelophehad came before Eleazar the priest, Joshua, and the leaders, demanding their inheritance, following up on what they had presented in Numbers 27:2.
Eleazar the priest, Joshua, and the heads of the tribes distributed the inheritance at Shiloh by the tabernacle, a setting similar to that in Numbers 27:2.
